title: What each command gives its job
prompt: The scheduler's job commands arrive as text, one `spark-submit` command per line, in the `value` column of `application_logs_raw`. Write `solve(application_logs_raw)` so it returns one row per command: the script, the application name, the master and the shuffle partitions the job will get, and how many arguments the script receives.
rules: Each line is `spark-submit`, then options, each option followed by exactly one value (`--master local[2]`, `--conf key=value`), then the script and its arguments. Words are separated by single spaces.
The script is the first word that is neither an option nor an option's value. Every word after it goes to the script, even one that looks like an option.
When an option is given twice, the last one wins; for `--conf`, the last value of the same key wins.

With no `--name`, the application is named after the script's file name (`jobs/report.py` gives `report.py`). With no `--master`, the master is `local[*]`. With no `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions`, it's `200`.
Columns, in order: `script`, `app_name`, `master`, `shuffle_partitions` (text) and `args` (a whole number of type `int`). Keep duplicate commands; an empty table gives no rows.
hints: Walk the words after `spark-submit` two at a time while the word starts with `--`; the first word that doesn't is the script.
Keep the options in a dictionary as you go, so a later value replaces an earlier one. Split a `--conf` value at its first `=`.
A `.py` word can be an option's value (`--py-files libs/rules.py`), so don't look for the script by its extension.
explanation: This is how `spark-submit` itself reads a command: option and value pairs up to the first word that isn't an option, which is the script; the rest is `sys.argv[1:]`. In the sample, `jobs/errors.py --name late-errors --master yarn` runs as `errors.py` on `local[2]` with 4 arguments, because the options after the script belong to the script. A repeated option or `--conf` key simply overwrites the earlier one, so the 16 partitions and `local[3]` win. The defaults come from Spark when nothing sets them: the script's file name, `local[*]` and 200 shuffle partitions. Searching the whole line for `--master` or for the first `.py` word gets the fourth sample command wrong.
